evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep skips straight to pulling up the date and asking questions without framing the call length, quote dependability, or waiting for an explicit yes. Only after several exchanges does he say 'it'll be about ten minutes or so does that work for you?' — reactive, not proactive framing.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Name asked (Lisa Deleon), moving date asked (October 15th), city-to-city route asked (San Antonio to unspecified destination — destination address never confirmed), apartment size asked indirectly (2-bedroom confirmed). Destination city/address never established.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked after probing has already started: 'Anything in particular about the move right at the moment you're concerned about and wanted me to address.' This comes after he's already asked for name, date, and pulled up the date in the system.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raises a major concern: 'last time we got movers are mostly everything was broken including our TVs.' Rep acknowledges with insurance pitch but does not dig deeper — no 'tell me more about that' or follow-up question to understand what specifically happened or what would alleviate that fear beyond the damage coverage pitch.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No reflection or summary of the customer's stated concern. Rep pivots directly to the damage coverage benefit without mirroring back what he heard.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (apartment) confirmed, floor (second floor) confirmed, number of rooms (2 bedroom) confirmed, furniture items clarified through probing. Missing: walking distance to building/stairs, additional stops/secondary destination details, special considerations explicitly asked. Partial credit — roughly half the standard logistics checklist covered.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Not offered. Rep discusses the impact of unpacked miscellaneous items but never asks 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?'
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Yes — 'typically we see about 25 to thirty boxes for a two bedroom apartment. Do you think that'll be about right for you?' and later 'And then how many boxes do you think you'll have?'
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Full anchor present. Rep gives typical range ('three and a half and five and a half hours with two guys... between $812 and $1,196') and personalizes to this customer's specifics ('You have a lot less furniture than normal but actually a few more boxes than typical second floor, fourth floor elevator. So, about $812 to $1,004').
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Full disclosure of trip fee ($140), hourly rate ($192/two-man crew), minimum ($620 for 2.5 hours), billing increments (15-minute), and includes-in-rate framing ('pad and shrink wrap, any of the furniture items... tools... fully insured... no taxes, no credit card fees'). Strong transparency.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. After delivering the estimate and promise details, rep asks 'As far as that goes any questions on any of that' — a standard questions check, not 'Does that feel fair?' and no pause follows; customer immediately responds.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Partial. Rep mentions 'we do have on time guarantees if we're ever late... we do discount your money back' but does not clearly state the discount terms or when the discount kicks in — vague on the actual benefit structure.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Partial. Rep mentions 'No Worries Damage Coverage' and '$2,000 per move... above and beyond the industry standard which is 60¢ per pound' but does not explicitly state 'no deductible / no fine print' and the framing that it is 'built into the rate, not an add-on' is present ('included in our hourly rate') but not as clear and direct as the rubric expects.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No. After the Two Promises section, rep pivots directly to 'As far as that goes any questions on any of that' without asking a version of 'Does that put those to rest?' or confirming the customer feels assured.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Throwaway. Rep asks 'As far as that goes any questions on any of that' — a generic 'any questions' with no genuine specificity like 'What's still concerning you about this move?' Customer does not raise anything, so no follow-up needed.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Not asked. No version of 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' is present.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never asked. Rep never says 'Would you like our help with your move?' or any direct booking ask. Instead, he says 'I can send an email with the quote and yeah, if you want to move forward with that, you can just respond back to the email' — all contingency and no direct ask.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Not mentioned. No mention of rate lock or holding the price.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Rep confirms apartment address (7999 Pono Road, San Antonio, second floor) and that he will send an email quote. Missing: destination address, phone number, arrival window, crew size (implied as 2-man crew but not explicitly confirmed at booking), and no notes taken about the customer's damage concern for the crew.
evidence_quotes.customer_destination: Never established — customer states pickup location but no destination address or city is confirmed.

top_strength: Calvin delivered a transparent, well-structured estimate with clear pricing anchor, trip fee, hourly rate, minimum, and billing terms that directly addressed the move's logistics.
coaching_note: Calvin must ask 'Would you like our help with your move?' directly and wait for a yes before closing — he gave away the booking ask and sent the customer to email response instead, eliminating urgency and control of the next step.
